chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Idrees ibn Abdullah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a newborn who is born and then dies on the seventh day, should Aqeeqa be performed for him? He (peace be upon him) said: If he dies before midday, Aqeeqa is not performed for him, and if he dies after midday, Aqeeqa is performed for him.

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdullah (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الظُّهْرِ: Midday (the specific time boundary for the ruling)
key_terms.يُعَقُّ: Aqeeqa (ritual sacrifice performed on the seventh day for a newborn)

ai.seo_question: When should Aqeeqa be performed for a child who dies before the seventh day?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the jurisprudential nuance of Aqeeqa for infants dying within the first week, establishing a critical temporal threshold at midday (Zohr) to determine the obligation. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of linking ritual duties to specific stages of life, treating the period after midday as sufficient for the child to be considered a distinct entity entitled to the sacrifice. It highlights the precision with which early Imams applied legal principles to the delicate matter of infant mortality.
